Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

convince verb

also persuade, be convinced, I’m convinced, be sure (of), talk someone into

classical

Cic. Att. 1.5.8: tibi persuādeās tē ā mē frāternē amārī
Sen. Ep. 108.22: nec difficulter mihi ut inciperem melius cēnāre persuāsit

persuādeō, persuādēre, persuāsī, persuāsum

verb, second conjugation, with a dative of the person; accusative and infinitive for “convince that”, ut or nē + subjunctive for “persuade to”

convince (that); persuade (to)

The person convinced is in the dative, so the passive is impersonal: mihi persuāsum est, I am convinced; mihi persuādērī numquam potuit, I could never be convinced (Cic. Sen. 80). Tibi persuādeās, “be sure”, closes Cicero’s letters to his family.

Other words

  • persuāsum habeō — I am convinced, I hold it as settled

    phrase; with an accusative and infinitive, often with sibi · also used · classical · Caes. B.G. 3.2: sibi persuāsum habēbant (Lewis & Short)

    A settled conviction, as in Caesar; for the moment of being won over, mihi persuāsum est.

  • fidem faciō (alicui) — make (someone) believe, win belief

    phrase; often with an accusative and infinitive · also used · classical · Cic. Brut. 187: fidem facit ōrātiō (Lewis & Short)

    Of what wins belief, a speech or an argument; the person is in the dative.

  • convincō, convincere, convīcī, convictum — prove (someone) wrong or guilty; refute

    verb, third conjugation · avoid · classical

    Not “convince”: classically to convict of a crime or an error, or to prove a thing beyond doubt (Lewis & Short; see prove).

Examples

  • cūrā ut valeās et nōs amēs et tibi persuādeās tē ā mē frāternē amārī

    look after yourself, love us, and be sure that I love you as a brotherCic. Att. 1.5.8

  • cūrā ut valeās et ita tibi persuādeās, mihi tē cārius nihil esse nec umquam fuisse

    take care of yourself, and be sure that nothing is dearer to me than you, or ever wasCic. Fam. 14.3.5

  • patre itaque meō rogante … ad prīstinam cōnsuētūdinem rediī; nec difficulter mihi ut inciperem melius cēnāre persuāsit

    so at my father’s request … I went back to my old habit; he had no trouble persuading me to start dining betterSen. Ep. 108.22

See also confirm, prove, believe, argument.

SourcesLewis & Short: persuadeo · Lewis & Short: fides · Lewis & Short: convinco
